Aerial Wildlife 
Survey Report 
Wildlife Management Unit 346 Ungulate Aerial Survey (2018) 
 
 
Background 
Wildlife Management Unit (WMU) 346 is a largely mixed wood and conifer forested unit with agriculture along the 
east side of the WMU. Traditionally WMU 346 has had high to medium densities of moose and other ungulates.  
The last survey conducted for a moose population estimate was in winter of 2012/13 using the Distance 
methodology. The previous survey was also the first attempt to estimate populations of white -tail deer. Antlered 
moose are managed on a limited entry hunt with an archery only A25-S23 season and general S24-O31 and N1-
N30 seasons. There is no antlerless moose season.  Mule deer (antlered) are also managed through a limited 
entry hunt S17-N30 and a general archery only A25-S16 season.  White-tailed deer (antlered and antlerless) are 
managed by a general archery only A25-S16 season and a general S17-N30 season; up until 2015 two 
supplemental antlerless white-tailed deer tags could also be acquired, however, this has currently been reduced to 
one tag. 
 
Survey Method 
The objective of this survey was to establish population estimates for moose, white-tailed and mule deer; including 
age and sex classifications where possible. Transects, up to 10 km in length and oriented north-south, were 
established spatially throughout the WMU at 2 km intervals within a GIS environment. Transects were randomly 
selected until 1903 kilometres of survey distance was achieved. The survey was then flown using distance 
sampling methodology as described in the Distance Sampling Chapter of the Aerial Ungulate Survey Protoc ol 
Manual (ESRD, 2014). 
 
Results 
The survey was completed from February 20-22, 2018. Total ungulates observed were 176 moose, 87 white-tailed 
deer, 7 mule deer and 320 elk observed. Moose were observed in 114 groups and white -tailed in 24 groups. Mule 
deer groups were insufficient to estimate population. Of the 176 moose that were successfully classified, 96 were 
cows, 47 were calves, 32 were bulls and 1 was unclassified.  Due to most white-tailed and mule deer bucks having 
dropped their antlers, a sex ratio was not possible. Historical and current population estimates and species 
densities are presented in Table 1. Of the 320 elk observed, 94 were cows, 33 were calves, 23 were bulls and 170 
were unclassified. During this survey, deep snow depths likely kept many white-tail deer under conifer cover.
